sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 is here, and we’re finally getting to see what Rockstar has been cooking up for the last decade-and-change. It may be a studio already famous for its unbridled attention to detail, but just how many more tiny flourishes, references, and opportunities for emergent hilarity has Rockstar stuffed into GTA 6? The answer is a lot, so let’s get straight to it: here are 99 incredible little details in Grand Theft Auto 6. And don’t worry, you’ll find no story spoilers here. 1. From the get-go, it appears Rockstar has left no box unchecked. That is, during the Prologue, there’s a strong chance you’ll be successfully captured by the VCPD before you can effect a getaway. However, if you do manage to escape, you’ll get an extra segment of gameplay after the prison counselor addresses your initial evasion, in which she may even name-check the vehicle you used. 2. GTA 6’s selection of radio stations and podcasts is fabulous, and massively stocked with songs. Want to hear them when you’re outside of a car? You can purchase earbuds at an electronics store so that you can tune in via your phone. 3. Blood stains remain in the world for multiple days, so you may well receive a reminder of some poor behaviour on your part, even after sleeping and returning to the same spot in the days that follow. 4. Gang hideouts will reveal themselves all over the map as you progress, but one of the first you’ll probably find is an illegal animal smuggling operation tucked away in Jason’s hometown. Make sure you listen to the parrot for a clue to find more loot. 5. Speaking of animals, keep in mind that dogs will protect their owners, so consider that before you insult anyone out walking their best friend. 6. It’s also common to come across animals fighting amongst themselves, but if you spook them, they’ll typically scarper. 7. And no, it doesn’t appear that crocodiles take much interest in unconscious people that you may dump near them. But when they wake up, all bets are off. 8. The highly impressive blood tech will realistically coat surfaces the claret touches, such as covering a croc’s snout after snacking on an unfortunate fellow’s head. 9. Don’t park your car too close to the basketball hoop outside Jason’s first house. Even a well-placed shot could smash the windows of your ride. 10. Of course, cars can suffer considerably more than a busted windscreen, and car damage in GTA 6 is ludicrously good. Panels buckle dramatically, parts fall off, and dents appear exactly where they should. 11. Lose a wheel and the unfortunate rotor scraping against the asphalt will glow bright red as it dramatically heats up. 12. There’s a distinct difference in paint quality between hasty Pay ’n’ Spray jobs and professional recoats at a dedicated auto shop. Pay ’n’ Sprays offer extremely limited colours, and the paint finish has a noticeable “orange peel” effect. 13. Car glass isn’t perfect and, in the right light, you can see lots of scuffs, scratches, and imperfections. 14. Wipers will even leave visible streaks on the glass during rain, even though that’s something you’d only ever see rarely in the first-person view. 15. Businesses have their own vehicles, and you’ll spot vans and trucks across the map with all kinds of corporate and small business logos plastered on them. We’re still seeing ones we haven’t noticed, even after 120 hours, and it greatly increases the feeling of vehicle variety on the road. 16. The details on cars even extend to the fact that they have animated drivetrains – you can more easily spot when you flip a car, so take this as an excuse to get a little chaotic. 17. Some cars even have under-door lighting – an incredibly subtle effect you may well only occasionally see at night. 18. Brakes glow as a result of heavy use. 19. Superchargers make a very distinct noise, and your engine will sound different once you install them. 20. Vehicles have functioning indicators and windows, and you may even spot NPCs rolling up their windows if you’re annoying them. To use your own blinkers, tap left and right on the D-pad. 21. Truck nuts on vehicles. That’s it. No, they don’t shrink in the cold, but I’m not holding that against it. 22. Alongside the massive number of regular vehicles to discover, there are many unique vehicles sporting huge, custom decorations to find. One is a bright pink fan for a seafood restaurant that has “Our Shrimp so Pimp” painted on it. 23. There are also much, much cooler examples, including a very, very familiar Fast and Furious-adjacent green sports car with a custom paint job, tucked away in the largest house on Vespucci Island. The plate is the perfect touch, too: HAD YOU. 24. Like the cars, boats have also been lavished with attention to detail, and are typically christened with their own individual names, just like in real life. 25. And on that note, boats can now be physically launched from boat trailers, retrieved from the water again, and towed to anywhere else on the map. Same goes for jet skis and kayaks. 26. Cars and motorcycles can also be manually loaded onto trailers and towed anywhere you want. It doesn’t get around the tracker system, so it isn’t a method to cheat the new security features, but it’s still fun to fool around with. 27. Not only are jumbo jets way, way more authentically scaled – seriously, they’re huge now – but you need to enter them physically and walk to the cockpit to fly them. 28. Hijacking an enormous commercial airliner isn’t a thing the authorities will ignore or quickly forget. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 5 protagonists are referenced in a perfect GTA 6 Easter egg all about the events of Los Santos
sources.text: The Grand Theft Auto series has a propensity for memorable protagonists. Tommy Vercetti in Vice City, CJ in San Andreas, and Niko Bellic in 4 are key to what makes their respective entries so beloved. The same is true for Michael, Franklin, and Trevor regarding 5, and it should come as no surprise that GTA 6 pays an all-too-appropriate nod to the trio who led the previous entry in the series. While driving around Leonida and enjoying the podcast Vice City True Stories, you'll eventually start hearing about a few familiar names. It's a true crime podcast, because of course it is, and one of the subjects is a certain bank heist you'll know plenty about if you've completed the main story of Grand Theft Auto 5. Specifically, Trevor's pal Wade Hebert, and the suspicious deaths of Floyd and Deborah. The hosts are skeptical of his connection to Trevor, and how protective he was of Trevor's two partners in crime. A whole segment's been clipped on Twitter by DiscussingFilm if you can't play just now. "Could it be that the photograph was actually of three dangerous criminals? Criminals who knew how to handle a knife or a gun?" the host ponders. "Taking out Floyd and Deborah might have been as easy for them as it is for me to take no notice of failed auditions or final demands for payment." Oh, you don't know the half of it. These three men made Los Santos their playground, and they did it over and over again for years - though for you it would've been a much shorter period of time. "There were so many more questions about Michael, Franklin, and Wade's BFF," she continues. "What did Wade mean about robbing all them banks?" What did he mean, indeed. It's a delightfully meta way to tie the two games together, setting things up for further elaboration whenever Rockstar wants to go deeper. Since the game has podcasts, I hope the intention is to continue recording episodes and keep the radio selection updated. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more When you have over two billion US dollars in revenue right at launch, that kind of investment seems easy. Even if that's not what happens, it's good someone's scoping out the activities of those three. They aren't to be trusted, no matter how friendly they can come across. sources.title: Florida Joker gets his wish: He's a 'special voice actor' in Grand Theft Auto 6
sources.text: Looks like Lawrence Sullivan settled his differences with Rockstar. Remember in the closing days of 2023, when Rockstar dropped the first trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6 ? Amidst the everything it had going on was a brief shot of a man with extensive facial tattoos, who was quickly called out by people hip to such things as a knockoff of Florida Joker, aka Lawrence Sullivan, a Florida man who went viral for his 2017 mug shot . Sullivan himself called it out in a since-deleted TikTok video, first telling Rockstar " we gotta talk " and then, with no response forthcoming, threatening legal action . Not long after that, though, he put forth a new offer: " Let me voice the character , give me more storyline in the game… Let's make history happen, man." It seems that Sullivan got what he wanted: In a video posted to Instagram, Sullivan said he was given a role in GTA 6 . "I'm an official voice actor on GTA 6, the game." Sullivan says. "For the last three years a lot of people were saying I was not going to be in the game, I was not going to be nothing, they were destroying my mental health. They were saying a lot of fucked shit. But now it's time for me to shit on them and show them what the fuck Florida Joker is about!" "Y'all gonna see. Special voice actor for GTA 6. This ain't no gimmick, this ain't no lie!" I had doubts, but this apparently really ain't no gimmick or lie. Rockstar has posted the full GTA 6 credits and sure enough, Lawrence Sullivan is in there. Now, it could be a different Lawrence Sullivan, sure, but under the circumstances I don't think that's very likely. Sullivan's role doesn't appear to be a particularly prominent one: He's credited, along with a great many other people, as one of "The Local Population." But at the end of the day, he made it: Florida Joker really is in GTA 6, and he seems pretty chuffed about it. I'd call that a happy ending. sources.title: What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question
sources.text: "We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us." What would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors? That's the question Soldat and King Arthur's Gold developer Transhuman asked when it started working on 2024's roguelite shooter Maniac. The result is a delight, yet Maniac remains frustratingly underappreciated. Your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero. Throughout that time, your secondary objective is to create as much mayhem as possible - painting the road with the blood of your foes, slamming cars into buildings, performing drive-bys as you rampage across the procedurally-generated city. The more carnage you cause, the higher your Wanted level, until you're fending off police and the military. Maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock new characters, progressing a little further each time. It's a relatively slight experience, as its £4 price tag reflects, featuring a single compact map, just six characters, and barely any permanent progression. But Maniac makes a spirited argument for a return to a simpler time when GTA was all about shooting cops, stealing cars, and indiscriminately murdering pedestrians rather than the 'everything' game it is today. Maniac is also a game that feels like it's trying to make good on an idea many of us had when we first played GTA 1 & 2 all those years ago: what would a better-looking, more advanced version of that look like? And for developer Michał Marcinkowski, Maniac's genesis also harkens back to an earlier time. "When I was 12, I used to come back from school and play the demo of GTA 1," he tells me over email. "It was top-down and time-limited, and all I'd do was try to cause as much chaos as possible within the 20 minutes of the demo." And there's perhaps a hint of a 12-year-old's exuberance to Maniac. There's the bright colour palette and gleeful chaos of its physics-driven mechanics, the adrenaline rush its aggressive enemy AI creates, and its absurd roster of playable characters, which range from Little Girl to Hotdog Guy. "Each [character] is a bit of me and a bit of you," Marcinkowski explains. "We all have a drunk Santa in us. We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us. Each character failed at something and is lashing out." As each new Grand Theft Auto game pushes further into realism, the idea of recreating the rampages seen in classic GTA feels increasingly unpalatable, but Maniac's colourful cartoon aesthetic means it can get away with more. One Achievement, with a flourish of old-school bad-taste humour, challenges players to destroy five school buses using an airstrike ability called Santa's Little Helpers. And that level of irreverent, chaotic lunacy escalates the deeper into each session you get, particularly as your Wanted level climbs: if you antagonise law enforcement enough here, they eventually break out a game-ending nuke. "This comes back to being 12," Marcinkowski says. "Nukes are just cool. I wanted the game to end with a bang, and what's more maniacal and exaggerated than a nuke? So that idea was with me for more than 20 years." Core to Maniac's design is the ability to change from a Survivors-like auto-shooter to a standard shooter where you're able to control your aim. The latter option is, I think, the more fitting one, particularly given how much driving you do. If you squint, it almost feels like a GTA 2 clone. And while the Vampire Survivors inspirations are plentiful - including its now-standard three-option upgrade system - the GTA elements are clearly the more prevalent. It might not play exactly like a GTA game, but it certainly captures the series' early days spirit. And Marcinkowski says he's surprised more developers haven't tried to riff on GTA: "You'd expect the most popular game in the world to have hundreds of clones, but that's not the case." There may be a reason for that. As big as modern-day GTA is, clones are apparently much less popular. "When you look at the sales data, particularly of top-down GTA clones, they don't sell well", explains Marcinkowski. "I found that out way too late, and I thought Maniac wouldn't be a hit." His publisher was initially equally buoyant too. "But then they studied the market and stopped being so hyped. That's how it felt as we got close to release. The wishlist count wasn't very high." "I was expecting 10,000 [copies sold]," Marcinkowski tells me. "I actually started making another game two months before Maniac came out because I thought I'd go broke." But then the game launched, and early worries proved unfounded. It sold more than 100K copies, comfortably blowing past its maker's modest expectations, putting it in the top one percent of games released on Steam. It's a surprise success story built on the foundations of Marcinkowski's youth, and as we chat about GTA, he reveals he's less keen on Rockstar's modern games, which lack that classic gameplay drive. "I always liked the counter-culture side of GTA, which is why I put so much of it into Maniac," he elaborates. " GTA 6 seems to have become pop culture, so it's lost its appeal for me." Marcinkowski's heart, it seems, is old-school.

sources.title: Expedition 33 lead writer says Grand Theft Auto 6 layoff concerns show that 'people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value'
sources.text: "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing". Grand Theft Auto 6 is already enormously successful, having enjoyed "the biggest entertainment launch in history" . But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6 's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off." It might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one. It's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This issue was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July , claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 launches. "99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team." Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction." Svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector. "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created." sources.title: How to Get Ready for November 19
sources.text: November 19, 2026, has long been circled on your calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your XBOX console. We can hardly believe it’s almost here, either. Once midnight strikes, you want to be locked in the action, so to help you prepare, we created a checklist to ensure distractions are put to bed so you can settle in for a season of gaming like nothing you’ve ever experienced before. 2026 has been full of some absolute bangers: Gears of War E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Forza Horizon 6, Halo: Campaign Evolved, Minecraft Dungeons II, Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred , Control Resonant , Mixtape , Pragmata , The Blood of Dawnwalker , Star Wars: Galactic Racer , 007 First Light , Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve … seriously, all these games came out this year . That also means you might have a hard drive that is nearing capacity. And you will be faced with some hard choices to free up approximately 212GB of space on your XBOX Series X|S before November 19. You could always upgrade the capacity of your console to keep all your games at the ready, using the storage expansion slot on the back of the console. Otherwise, you’ll have a hard choice to make which we do not envy. But know that you’re in good company – we had to find a way to make room too. XBOX Cloud Gaming means that you don’t need to own an XBOX Series X|S console to experience the latest games (or use up that hard drive space) – you can stream directly from the cloud to your XBOX One console. Game Pass subscribers receive an allotment of hours per month as part of their plans, but you can also purchase blocks of time . Certain upcoming major releases have been confirmed as cloud-ready on day one , so even if you don’t own a current gen console, your latest obsession isn’t out of reach. You never want to settle in for a long gaming session only to immediately get hit with an update download. If you haven’t used your XBOX Series X|S or XBOX One in a minute, be sure to power up and connect to the internet beforehand and make sure you’re all set with the latest system updates. You can also install any upcoming releases you may have pre-ordered, while you’re at it. If you’re feeling a gaming flu coming on (and there’s a lot of that going around right now), then take a sick day, rather than risk infecting your coworkers or classmates. Sometimes you just need to listen to your body’s needs, relax, and let the fever run its course. Miami’s own DJ Khaled, aka Dr. XBOX will write you a personalized note to help explain the situation. If this thing is really serious, you may even need the whole week to recover – it’s the responsible thing to do. We all have responsibilities. Some of them come with four legs and a suspect bladder. Don’t let Rufus ruin your gaming fun. Get ahold of a local dog walker to take them outside so you can enjoy the big day uninterrupted. Or drop them off at doggie daycare for a day (or week) to get them out of your hair. Is your XBOX in an area of the house that is easily accessible to younger players? Consider the steps you need to take to get it out of younger sightlines, like running an extension cable out to the shed in the backyard or huddling up in your at-home office. Even if you do find yourself bouncing between rooms, your save files reside in the Cloud, allowing you to pick up your session wherever you last plugged your console in. We’re always on the hunt for new tunes and one of the things we’re most looking forward to on November 19 is discovering a whole bunch of new tracks that are sure to make our listening playlist pop throughout the year. You can get started here on Spotify . XBOX Design Lab lets you create your own next-gen XBOX Wireless Controller. Choose from a combination of colors, patterns, textured grips, and more. You could even pick up some specially themed versions of controllers styled in hot pink and pastels – this one is particularly striking . Speaking of controllers, if you expect long gaming sessions in your near future, make sure that it’s plugged in so it has a full charge when you need it, or stock up on AA batteries. Maybe even get a backup controller ready so you can hot-swap them in and minimize interruptions. Looking for something to add to your queue? Check out the 1967 classic, “Bonnie and Clyde,” featuring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway to get you in the mood for an epic story about two tragic lovers who fall into a life of crime. We’ll have to wait and see if the outcome is any different this time around starting on November 19.

sources.text: You can fly a GTA 6 jet right at the start of the game by raiding the nearby military base, and here's how to do it Knowing how to get a jet in GTA 6 is essential information if you're planning to cause chaos, as taking control of one of these military aircraft is considered peak criminal behavior. While you'd expect that significant progress in GTA 6 would be required before you even had a chance of swiping such high-end hardware, you can actually go and help yourself to one pretty much as soon as you start the game. To try it yourself, here's how to steal a jet in GTA 6. The location for a number of GTA 6 jets is the Mile Zero Air Station, which is found by heading west along the main road from the starting area, through Abismo Key, then on to Southwind and the military base itself. You can drive there in any vehicle, though I recommend not using your GTA 6 personal vehicle as it will get trashed and left inside the base, so steal a sturdy and reasonably fast vehicle for the job. Purchasing and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation will also improve your odds of surviving the initial stage. Follow the route marked on my map above, which will lead you through some barriers on the road to a set of soldiers who will open fire, then take the first turning right and drive through more soldiers until you see a dirt pile ahead that you can hit to clear the security fences. This is also a Stunt Jump, though you don't need to complete it as long as you clear the perimeter and land on the runway. Once on the runway inside the miliary base, drive straight ahead to where you'll see several GTA 6 jets parked up next to hangars. Pull up alongside one, jump out of your car and hop straight into the cockpit, before firing up the afterburner and turning onto the runway to take off. Once you've taken control of your jet and got airborne, follow the prompt to retract the landing gear and you're away! Be aware that you'll have attracted at least a five-star GTA 6 Wanted Level with this theft, which could go up to six if you start blowing things up, so multiple military jets will be scrambled to shoot you down with homing missiles. I was barely able to reach the first bridge before getting blown out of the sky, but if you fly low and take evasive action you may fare better – good luck! If you're looking for an impressive ride that's easier to obtain then here's how to steal the GTA 6 Paul Walker car , which you can then use to arrive in style at the various GTA 6 Strip Club locations around Leonida. sources.text: Finding the Slim Jim in Chapter 2 is essential if you want to get better at stealing vehicles Stealing cars in GTA 6 is one of the easiest ways to attract attention from the police, thanks to the new Wanted system. This essential carjacking tool will unlock as part of the main GTA 6 mission list , coming into your possession after you begin a quest called ' Moses '. sources.text: The GTA 6 Snap Tool is an essential item which lets you get into locked doors without setting off alarms Breaking and entering is more complicated than it's ever been before in a Grand Theft Auto game. You never know what's behind a locked door – cash to be grabbed, narcotics to be fences, safes to be broken into. The problem is that breaking open doors creates a lot of noise, and will set off alarms. Thankfully, there is another way. All you need is to find the Snap Gun in GTA 6. The Snap Gun is a lockpicking device that can be acquired by progressing through the main story, and it's perhaps the most important piece of equipment in the game (beating out the Slim Jim and the Key Cloner ). Below I'm going to walk you through how to get the GTA 6 Snap Gun and how to use it. The Snap Gun is locked behind progression. You'll need to complete Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3, a fence-specific GTA 6 mission that unlocks after you've completed Boobie Time. You'll be introduced to Yasmani, one of the key vendors in GTA 6 who will pay a premium for marked bills and jewellery you've stolen. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that Jason and Lucia can properly assist in a few heists of high-end jewellery stores in Vice City. If a door is locked, there's a very good chance that you can use the Snap Gun to open it. Walk up to a door and, rather than pressing Square/X to break it open, press Triangle/Y instead. This will let you use the Snap Gun, where you're then required to use the left analogue stick to find the sweet spot and then pump the right-trigger until a meter fills. You'll hear the click when the lock is picked. The Snap Gun is particularly useful when you're robbing Pawn Shops, Jewellery stores, and other key locations – so long as you've already threatened the clerks and guards to stay still while you work. The Snap gun circumvents alarm systems installed in stores to monitor the door. It's worth noting here that in certain locations that carry a lot of cash or valuables, a Snap Gun won't be enough. If you walk up to a door and it's only asking for explosives, then a sticky bomb or grenade is what's required – just prepared for the alarms to go off and for the cops to be in hot pursuit. sources.text: GTA 6 é bom? Confira a review do aguardado Grand Theft Auto VI Após 13 longos anos, a espera finalmente acabou: GTA 6 está disponível em todo o mundo no PS5 e no Xbox Series X|S . Com isso, muitos jogadores já devem estar se perguntando como trocar de personagens no jogo — e o VOXL vai te explicar a seguir. GTA 6 permite alternar entre Jason e Lucia durante o gameplay, mas a troca manual de protagonistas não fica disponível logo no início da campanha. O recurso é desbloqueado conforme o jogador avança na história e pode ser ativado por um comando simples no controle. Embora os dois personagens apareçam desde os primeiros momentos da narrativa, boa parte do Capítulo 1 é dedicada a missões específicas. A possibilidade de explorar o mundo aberto com qualquer um dos protagonistas chega mais adiante na aventura. No início de GTA 6 , Lucia está presa, o que impede o jogador de explorar o mapa livremente com ela. Depois que você completar a missão “Pescando” com Jason, o mundo aberto é liberado — mas ainda não é possível alternar manualmente entre os protagonistas. A primeira missão em que Jason e Lucia aparecem juntos é “Libertação Diurna”. Após concluí-la, o controle volta para Jason, já que Lucia precisa cumprir as condições de sua liberdade condicional. Outras atividades do Capítulo 1 também permitem jogar com Lucia, como “Armadilha para Turistas”. No entanto, a troca livre só fica disponível depois de concluir esse capítulo e avançar pelos acontecimentos iniciais do Capítulo 2. A partir daí, basta pressionar a seta para a direita no direcional digital (D-pad) para alternar entre Jason e Lucia. Caso o retrato de um dos protagonistas apareça acinzentado, significa que ele está indisponível por algum motivo dentro da narrativa, como estar ocupado em outra missão. Também pode acontecer de o personagem que acabou de ser substituído chamar um RydeMe e deixar a região. Durante esse período, o menu de troca pode ficar temporariamente indisponível até que a situação seja resolvida. Um dos detalhes que chamam a atenção no sistema de troca de GTA 6 é a velocidade da transição entre Jason e Lucia. Nos consoles da nova geração, o processo leva cerca de 10 segundos e, em algumas situações, pode ser ainda mais rápido. Em GTA 5 , alternar entre Michael, Trevor e Franklin podia levar mais tempo no PS3 e no Xbox 360 — plataformas que não contavam com SSDs de alta velocidade. O problema foi reduzido na versão lançada para PS5, mas a nova aventura da Rockstar apresenta uma transição bastante ágil. O desempenho está relacionado ao SSD NVMe dos consoles atuais, que permite carregar os arquivos do jogo em alta velocidade. Com isso, a mudança entre os protagonistas acontece em poucos segundos e não exige longas telas de carregamento. Outro detalhe é que Jason e Lucia continuam realizando atividades diferentes enquanto não estão sob controle do jogador. Em determinadas ocasiões, por exemplo, Jason pode aparecer praticando tiro ao alvo com latinhas em uma ponte — enquanto outras situações mostram os personagens envolvidos em atividades próprias pelo mapa. Você já começou sua aventura com Jason e Lucia? Comente nas redes sociais do Voxel o que está achando de GTA 6 e conte qual dos protagonistas está sendo seu favorito até agora. sources.title: Rockstar wants you to see yourself in GTA 6's Jason and Lucia
sources.text: "We might all be better off when we're together and not going it alone." GTA 6 's Jason and Lucia might be hardened criminals, but Rockstar Games designed the couple to be relatable in other ways. As the studio's narrative lead explained, "we are all about two bits of bad luck away from completely losing it" in the real world. "Playing GTA 6, the main thing we want players to feel is connection. To Jason and Lucia, who they need to believe in and inhabit for this journey through the game, but then also that connection in the game between the two characters," senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained in quotes given to GamesRadar+. "Living in the actual world in this present moment, it feels like there is so much noise and so much pressure on everyone - politics, the environment, media, social media. It's coming at you from everywhere. It seems like we are all about two bits of bad luck away from completely losing it. That is the world we are showing you on the streets of Vice City and in the rest of Leonida - everyone's been driven to a kind of madness that comes out in lots of different ways, from conspiracy theories to self-help cults to get-rich-quick schemes and drug habits." GTA 6's main couple doesn't exactly have many options outside of the criminal ones, and I think the game does a good job at giving them some real, personal, human stakes to ground it all - making their occasional robberies and murders a tad more understandable. As the couple says in the game, the world is stacked against them. They can't get ahead by playing by the rules. Even so, GTA 6 still has an optimistic view on life in the modern era, which itself is a big departure from GTA 5's generally cynical world view: "With all that going on, we wanted to have two humans at the center of the story that the player can care about and see themselves in, and then this idea that maybe (however bad you are) we might all be better off when we're together and not going it alone." sources.text: GTA 6 é bom? Confira a review do aguardado Grand Theft Auto VI O lançamento de GTA 6 entrou para a história da indústria do entretenimento. Segundo um comunicado divulgado pela Take-Two Interactive nesta sexta-feira (20), o jogo da Rockstar Games arrecadou US$ 3,79 bilhões em vendas no primeiro dia , estabelecendo um novo recorde para lançamentos de entretenimento em qualquer mídia. Além da receita bilionária, a empresa revelou que Grand Theft Auto VI vendeu 32,5 milhões de cópias antes mesmo de seu lançamento oficial. O número representa um novo recorde de vendas antecipadas em todas as plataformas, de acordo com a publicadora. A Take-Two também destacou a recepção da crítica, apontando que GTA 6 alcançou nota 99 no Metacritic , garantindo a melhor avaliação da plataforma. Com os resultados, o novo capítulo da franquia supera marcas históricas que já pertenciam à própria série e consolida a estreia como um dos maiores acontecimentos comerciais da história dos videogames. O resultado coloca GTA 6 no topo dos maiores lançamentos da história do entretenimento. Para efeito de comparação, GTA 5, lançado em 2013, arrecadou US$ 1 bilhão nos primeiros três dias de disponibilidade, marca que também estabeleceu um recorde na época. O desempenho do novo jogo é ainda mais expressivo quando comparado ao cinema. Segundo informações do Business Insider , Vingadores: Ultimato, um dos maiores sucessos de bilheteria de todos os tempos, levou cinco dias para alcançar US$ 1 bilhão mundialmente. O jogo acompanha Jason e Lucia em uma história ambientada em Vice City e no estado fictício de Leonida, com uma trama que envolve crimes, conspirações e a relação entre os dois protagonistas. sources.title: How Rockstar Made Every NPC Feel Alive in GTA 6
sources.text: Game developers often refer to their open world cities as characters due to the sheer craftsmanship involved in building out a believable, diverse playspace for the player with its own districts, history, and architecture. This is truer for GTA 6 than most games, but what makes Leonida really feel alive — outside of the puddles of bin juice, the regional-specific cop cars, and mapped out power grid — are the people who live there. GTA 6 feels like a massive evolution in what it means to be a non-player character (NPC) because there’s an emphasis on the “C” — they’re actually characters in their own right. NPCs don’t just all look unique — with body types, skin, dress style, and hair making them stand apart — they have their own personalities and temperaments. Start a fight with one NPC and they might fight back, while another runs away. One could start a fight by slapping you, another might flick their cigarette at you or tip their drink over your head. Passersby can cheer the fight on, flee, or get involved. Some stop after a single punch knocks sense into them, while others swing until they’re out cold . No matter where you go in GTA 6, it feels like a lived-in world, on the macro and micro scale. There are over 100 interiors to explore, and each house tells you a story about its occupants. Listen to conversations out on the streets and you’ll get a window into their minds, built out by an entire Rockstar studio dedicated to making them authentic and believable, while still being larger-than-life, funny, and often unhinged. “A big part of it was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories,” said Steven Messinger, Rockstar's senior design director for the open world. “For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we’ve fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they’re distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer. “Players will only pick up on bits and pieces of this, but having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren’t there.” To build this tangible sense of place, Rockstar takes in-depth research trips for GTA games , embedding the writers in the mundane and the more extreme to really capture the soul of a city. Helicopter trips of the Florida Keys, ride-alongs with police, talking to people, taking photos and notes, all build up a snapshot that Rockstar bottles up to digitize in video game format. “We had a lot of fun trying to capture the raw energy and vibrant chaos that Florida is known for,” said senior design director of world and population, John Macpherson. “By immersing ourselves into a number of these locations on reference trips, spending time with locals, experiencing as much as possible firsthand, we gathered a direct sense of what would make Leonida feel truly alive. “Everywhere you look, little stories constantly unfold. It could be as simple as what someone’s wearing, how fit they are, how they walk and talk, who they’re with, what tunes they’re blasting as they cruise down the street. We tried to match that in-game as much as possible, hopefully resulting in something that feels full of life.” You can walk along Vice Beach and see sugar daddies with their trophy wives, locals playing volleyball, tourists sunbathing, and people walking their pets. Everywhere you look, there’s something happening in Leonida, and it’s completely enveloping. You feel like a part of its world, rather than a godlike being with total control over it. There’s a mission around the midpoint of the game where protagonists Jason and Lucia people-watch from a hotel sunbed, inventing backstories for the guests by the pool, and it’s something I found myself doing as I explored the world and passed people by, such is the variety and diversity of the game’s NPCs. No other game has ever had such a colorful cast of extras, which is wild when you consider all this was built to add credibility to a world you can zoom past at 100mph. “We evolved from monolithic NPCs built to visual standards that were lower than the main cast in GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, to fully fleshed-out characters with singular awareness and visual identities,” said Valmor Garcia, senior technical art director on GTA 6. “They are driven by dynamic moods, personalities, unique anatomy, facial features, and dialogue that are visually on par with our protagonists, Jason and Lucia.” Rockstar built entirely new technology for GTA 6 to simulate hair, cloth, and the way muscles move under the skin. All that work is implemented equally across all characters, so there’s never that uncanny moment where you come face-to-face with a flat and lifeless NPC, staring at you with dead eyes. Everyone you meet is equally detailed, and the range of visual design is staggering. Of course, this approach created challenges in other areas of development. It’s fairly straightforward to implement a combat system in a game where all character models are approximately the same size, but the varied body types of GTA 6 meant Rockstar had to take a look at how it approached animations so physical contact looks good no matter how big or small the character models are. Especially since this is a game where the two leads can also change in size through diet and exercise . “We decided early on that we wanted to really push the variation in character sizes and body types,” vice president of animation, Mark Tennant, explained. “This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat. “Developing this workflow meant that we needed our animators to adopt new tec

sources.text: GTA 6 é bom? Confira a review do aguardado Grand Theft Auto VI Um dos maiores vazamentos envolvendo GTA 6 ganhou um novo capítulo justamente após o lançamento do jogo. O hacker conhecido como Cyberleek voltou à ativa em 19 de novembro e afirma ter disponibilizado na internet uma versão de desenvolvimento do título para Xbox, com aproximadamente 209 GB. Segundo o grupo, a build corresponde a uma versão completa de novembro de 2026, mas ainda está sem o arquivo executável principal, necessário para iniciar o jogo. A estratégia também envolve uma nova tentativa de lucrar com uma criptomoeda própria, chamada $CYBERLEEK. A promessa é liberar o arquivo restante caso a moeda alcance uma capitalização de mercado de US$ 15 milhões. No entanto, mesmo sem atingir essa meta, o responsável pelos vazamentos afirma que pretende disponibilizar o executável em 23 de novembro. De acordo com informações publicadas pelo IGN , o Cyberleek anunciou que possui uma versão de desenvolvimento de GTA 6 destinada aos consoles Xbox. O material teria sido distribuído por torrent, mas a autenticidade e a integridade dos arquivos ainda não foram confirmadas de maneira independente pelo Kotaku. Em uma publicação, o responsável pelo perfil afirmou que a comunidade poderia conseguir emular o jogo no PC em aproximadamente uma semana, com desempenho superior a 30 FPS . Vale lembrar que GTA 6 foi desenvolvido para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S, com a Rockstar mirando 30 quadros por segundo nos consoles. O especialista em segurança cibernética VX Underground analisou os arquivos que circulam na internet e considerou que o material aparenta ser legítimo. Ainda assim, existem questionamentos técnicos sobre a integridade do pacote, incluindo a ausência de determinados arquivos de sistema que podem ser necessários para executar o jogo. A estratégia atual lembra bastante o que aconteceu em outubro , quando o Cyberleek condicionou a divulgação de uma versão de desenvolvimento de GTA 6 a uma capitalização de mercado de US$ 30 milhões para sua criptomoeda. Na ocasião, o perfil também publicou uma série de materiais supostamente extraídos do jogo, incluindo cenas de Lucia nua. Os vazamentos chamaram atenção pela quantidade de informações inéditas, mas a moeda perdeu valor e o responsável pela conta desapareceu novamente. Agora, a exigência foi reduzida para US$ 15 milhões. Segundo o IGN, a criptomoeda chegou a registrar uma capitalização de mercado de aproximadamente US$ 1,9 milhão após o novo anúncio, ainda muito distante do valor exigido. A movimentação também levantou alertas entre os fãs, que recomendam evitar qualquer investimento na moeda. Isso porque análises anteriores de transações indicaram que o responsável pelos vazamentos teria lucrado aproximadamente US$ 270 mil com operações envolvendo a criptomoeda em agosto. A possibilidade de uma versão de GTA 6 rodando no PC antes de um lançamento oficial da Rockstar também movimentou a comunidade de modders. Segundo o PC Gamer, alguns entusiastas acreditam que conseguirão executar o jogo em computadores pouco depois da divulgação do arquivo executável. O processo envolveria emulação e ferramentas capazes de recompilar os arquivos do Xbox para permitir a execução em outras plataformas. A publicação também destaca que tecnologias de inteligência artificial generativa podem ajudar a automatizar parte desse trabalho. Apesar das expectativas, ainda não existe garantia de que o projeto funcionará ou de que será possível reproduzir a experiência completa do jogo. A própria ausência de arquivos importantes no pacote divulgado pode representar um obstáculo para os responsáveis pela tentativa. Também existe uma questão jurídica: embora ferramentas de emulação não sejam necessariamente ilegais, distribuir ou baixar cópias não autorizadas de jogos protegidos por direitos autorais pode configurar violação de propriedade intelectual. O retorno do Cyberleek representa mais uma dor de cabeça para a Rockstar Games e sua controladora, a Take-Two Interactive. O grupo já havia divulgado materiais inéditos de GTA 6 meses antes do lançamento, levantando dúvidas sobre a segurança dos sistemas utilizados no desenvolvimento do jogo. Em agosto, a Take-Two iniciou uma investigação para identificar os responsáveis pelos vazamentos e chegou a solicitar intimações envolvendo plataformas como o Discord. Até agora, não está claro quem está por trás da conta Cyberleek ou como os arquivos teriam sido retirados dos ambientes internos da desenvolvedora. Na época, a Rockstar classificou o episódio como algo doloroso para a equipe de desenvolvimento e lamentou o impacto dos spoilers na experiência dos jogadores. A empresa também reforçou que os vazamentos não alterariam o cronograma de lançamento de GTA 6, que chegou oficialmente em 19 de novembro de 2026. Por enquanto, resta acompanhar se o executável prometido realmente será disponibilizado e se a comunidade conseguirá fazer a versão vazada funcionar. A Rockstar, conhecida por sua postura rigorosa contra violações de propriedade intelectual, também pode tomar medidas para impedir a circulação dos arquivos. sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Ubisoft merges two Creative Houses as H1 results decline 16.5%; Q2 net bookings above guidance thanks to Assassin's Creed Black Flag remake
sources.text: Ubisoft credits new Assassin's Creed leadership for enabling the game to "achieve an elevated level of quality and commercial performance" Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced increased Ubisoft's Q2 net bookings to €389 million, exceeding the estimated guidance of €370 million. Ubisoft stated that the new Assassin's Creed leadership within its Creative House structure "made clear, decisive choices in the final stretch of development," contributing to this outcome. "This enabled the game to achieve an elevated level of quality and a commercial performance that positions Black Flag Resynced among the industry's most successful action-adventure remakes," it said. Ubisoft's net bookings for H1, covering the six months ending September 30, 2026, declined 17% year-on-year to €645 million. The company maintained stable monthly active users and active players during the period, at 34 million and 88 million, respectively. In the associated report, Ubisoft announced that it had amended its Creative House structure by merging House 3 (focused on live service games) and 5 (focused on casual games) into a single unit to "leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms". The two units were already overseen by a single GM, Julian Bares; the firm said that the Creative House Structure was now "fully in place" with the remaining GM for Creative House 4 joining in January. It also established Motherbrain , a subsidiary focused on AI-driven "gameplay innovation", along with an unnamed dedicated business unit "to maximize the value of brands not included in a Creative House with an agile and investment-light model". The company stated its cost reduction program is "on track" and has entered the third phase. The fixed cost base for the period was €660 million, a 6% year-on-year decrease, with a target of €1.25 billion "on a run-rate basis" by March 2028. Ubisoft's headcount was down close to 1,100 over the period following layoffs and studio closures. Shortly before the earnings announcement it laid off 166 staff in its Montreal and Quebec studios , which followed the closure of studios in Winnipeg and Belgrade in June alongside job losses worldwide including at its San Francisco office , and subesquent layoffs at Ubisoft Barcelona in July. In Q2, Ubisoft's back-catalogue bookings declined 55% to €218 million, attributed to "a high comparison base that included partnerships and the significant contribution of Assassin's Creed Shadows." The Rainbow Six Siege franchise "performed in line with expectations" and has remained stable into the third quarter. However, Ubisoft announced the shutdown of Rainbow Six Mobile in October. During an earnings call (via Seeking Alpha ), CFO Frédérick Duguet said the decision was made because the company is "in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns" and "putting our resources on bigger opportunities". "Today, we can say that Console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises," Duguet continued. "Mobile is still an opportunity for the medium to longer term with games such as AC Jade on Assassin's Creed." "But the focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on Console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever." Tom Clancy's The Division 2 "saw net bookings growth this quarter, building on monetisation improvements initiated in Q1," while the Ghost Recon franchise "delivered a strong performance" during the period. "Our new operating model is now fully in place, with leadership secured across all Creative Houses," said Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot. "In an increasingly competitive entertainment industry, gamers require exceptional quality, distinctive creative experiences, uncompromising gameplay and a defined audience for games to stand out and succeed. "By repositioning our talents at the centre of decision-making and fostering a more spontaneous and direct link with our communities, our new model is designed precisely to deliver on these imperatives. Its first benefits are already visible, with the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and the renewed momentum of Rainbow Six Siege." Guillemot continued: "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organisation as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle. In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing plan with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months." "We are confirming our FY2026-27 objectives. By combining our iconic brands and creative talent with a more focused, agile and accountable operating model, we are building stronger Ubisoft."

sources.title: GTA 6 pode faturar R$ 11,8 bilhões no primeiro dia de lançamento
sources.text: O lançamento de GTA 6 deve gerar mais de US$ 2 bilhões (cerca de R$ 11,8 bilhões) em vendas no primeiro dia para a Take-Two Interactive. Com a dupla criminosa Lucia e Jason em uma jornada por Vice City, o novo jogo da Rockstar Games , subsidiária da Take-Two, caminha para estabelecer um recorde na indústria de games. Segundo estimativas da consultoria Sensor Tower até a noite de quinta-feira (19), o título soma 24,58 milhões de unidades vendidas, o que representa cerca de US$ 2,36 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 13,92 bilhões) em receita. O resultado equivale a quase três vezes os cerca de US$ 800 milhões (R$ 4,72 bilhões) arrecadados por GTA V em 2013, jogo amplamente considerado o maior lançamento de videogame em vendas nas primeiras 24 horas. Apesar de controlar franquias como Red Dead Redemption e NBA 2K, a Take-Two ainda é pouco conhecida do grande público. A empresa manteve uma postura reservada sobre a procura por GTA VI desde a abertura das pré-vendas, em junho, limitando-se a classificar a demanda como sem precedentes e muito acima das expectativas. Em teleconferência sobre os resultados financeiros no início deste mês, o CEO Strauss Zelnick reconheceu a empolgação dos consumidores e a recepção positiva da imprensa, mas evitou antecipar uma avaliação definitiva do lançamento. “O título é muito aguardado, os consumidores parecem muito, muito empolgados, e toda a imprensa até agora tem sido universalmente positiva, mas ainda não estamos prontos para declarar vitória”, afirmou. “Costumamos evitar proclamar sucesso antes que ele aconteça.” A Take-Two teria investido pelo menos US$ 1 bilhão (R$ 5,9 bilhões) na produção de GTA VI, colocando o projeto entre os mais caros da história do entretenimento. O investimento também foi acompanhado por uma ampla campanha de divulgação. Segundo a Sensor Tower, o trailer promocional GTA VI Extended Look, exibido na Netflix em agosto, ajudou a multiplicar por seis as pré-vendas. Perto do lançamento, a divulgação ganhou ações presenciais: em Miami, cidade que inspira Vice City, a equipe local da NBA realizou uma partida temática na quarta-feira para celebrar a chegada do jogo. As comemorações continuam no fim de semana com o GTA VI: The Festival, evento musical que terá apresentações da rapper vencedora do Grammy Cardi B, do produtor Metro Boomin e do rapper Travis Scott. Com a estreia do jogo, investidores aguardam informações sobre os planos da Take-Two para lançar GTA VI no PC e disponibilizar sua modalidade online. O componente multijogador é considerado crucial para transformar o título em uma fonte recorrente de receita. Parte dos analistas espera que a versão para computadores e o modo online cheguem em 2027. A corretora TD Cowen incluiu a Take-Two entre suas principais recomendações de investimento para aquele ano, enquanto o analista Doug Creutz demonstrou otimismo com as perspectivas financeiras da empresa após a estreia da modalidade. Para Creutz, o potencial de gastos recorrentes dos consumidores é um dos principais pontos a observar. Em sua avaliação, o tamanho e o momento de lançamento do próximo GTA Online são questões mais importantes para as ações da Take-Two do que o volume de unidades vendidas de GTA VI. sources.text: "We are but Promethean wanderers on the fringes of oblivion, clinging to a semblance of light amidst the vast abyss of our own ignorance. Voyaging uncharted waters may appear foolish to some, yet folly and heroism can often appear the same to the undiscerning eye," so says the voice of Johannes Zuch - creator, writer, director, composer, and 'perceptual architect' behind Leonida's latest favourite indie darling art game, Tenebrae Lux. It's pretentious, it's deeply up its own arse, and it's awkward and off-putting to play. A must-review for Eurogamer. Developed, seemingly single-handedly, by an eccentric developer called Johannes Zuch - auteur, pseud, charlatan - you first get introduced to this curious little experiment in one of GTA 6 's earliest missions, where protagonist Jason is forced to play it during a 'lad's night in' with buddy Cal. Jason is quick to dismiss Tenebrae Lux in company, but once Cal slinks off home - hungover and dreary - I slide the disc back into my JoyStation console and sink my teeth back into it. Jason loves this stuff, really. He only keeps Time Jackers: Rewind installed so his mates don't judge him. The first thing I notice about Tenebrae Lux is the name. It's Latin for 'darkness and light', or something similar. Is this riffing on Clair Obscur, which is French for 'light dark'? No, it's too cerebral for that - too plodding and navel-gazey. Sandfall Interactive wouldn't be this pretentious. Maybe it's a pastiche of Dear Esther , then, drawing on the tenets and schema of the 'walking simulator' genre and using that washed-out film noir aesthetic. But then, it's too wordy for that, with too many interactive and puzzle-adjacent elements. Ah, it must be mocking The Witness, instead - there's the telltale lighthouse, the 'I'm definitely not telling you where to go and what to do' internal narration, and of course the fingerprints of Johannes Zuch are all over it. Johannes Zuch, Jonathan Blow - see how they braided them together? (Sorry). Whilst this has been created by Rockstar as a pastiche - as much loving send-up as it is withering take down - and designed to make a quick joke in the early 'Feng Shui' mission, the game is playable from start to finish if you so desire. You boot it up by inserting a physical disc, too, which is funny given the context . And it's good! Well, not good good, but it's a proper brainteaser, and ribs 2016's The Witness with such knowledge and (I think?) respect that it's hard not to be charmed by Rockstar's game-within-a-game. There are collectibles to be found that riff on Mark Z. Danielewski's House of Leaves, too, a knowing nod to the most try-hard of all try-hard literature. Within seconds of the title screen, too, you're presented with a game-within-a-game-within-a-game. You must clear four boards filled with puzzle pieces as the protagonist mutters something mysterious and weird in his posh voice. Do so, and you unlock the door to the next location. Head up to a bunker, and you'll see a room filled with various clues - maybe it's a flashing lamp flickering in morse code, maybe it's a malfunctioning clock presenting a maths puzzle, maybe it's a pricetag on a record that changes on every visit, maybe it's a photograph with anomalous elements, maybe it's a "Developed Using Zuchworks Engine" easter egg hidden in the environment. You need to keep your wits about you, because one of these clues changes every time you enter - and the clue corresponds to a date that changes on a calendar on the wall. You can look up a guide if you need to, or you can spend far too long figuring out how all this relates to the telephone you can find in the room on your own, like muggins here, before opening up the path to the next puzzle. Look at the image below to see the level of record-keeping and brainteasing this bizarre little game prompted from me. I will say, the sense of achievement you get from playing around with this stuff is pretty remarkable, given - let's not forget I'm actually playing Grand Theft Auto 6 whilst I'm wandering around in the black and white murk trying to complete a puzzle game for no actual reward. The bunker room is, by far, the hardest part of Tenebrae Lux. From here, things ease up: you need to figure out the right sequence of glyphs on a bridge, and then put some distance between yourself and a curious and rather creepy suited man that's seemingly figuring things out ahead of you in a location inspired by, I think, The Backrooms (or Portal, or Superliminal, or maybe something else entirely. Who knows what Zuch was thinking?) "With the last enigma finally mastered," the narrator drones in his bumbling monotone, "I step forward into the void, the shadows swallow, consuming all, and then finally the sweet embrace of darkness of which there is no end." 'You have just experienced a Johannes Zuch experience', Tenebrae Lux tells me, before cutting to the best joke of the whole thing: the credits roll much akin to something Hideo Kojima would produce. So, what do you get out of all of this? Well - just like real puzzle games in the real world - nothing, really. If you've not completed one of the other three fully playable games in GTA 6, you will get a trophy/achievement. But given the main game is all about Jason and Lucia's desperate scramble to escape the poverty trap, to try and break free of the cycle of debt, violence, and consequence that keeps them clinging to Leonida's seedy underbelly, there's no monetary reward. There's no 'progress' in the sense of the protagonist's shared story. Even in terms of your own cold, hard, mathematical 'completion' you only need to boot each of the four games up once in order to work towards GTA 6's 100% completion. So what's the point of all this? Why did I spend the better part of 90 minutes trying to figure out how to find a sliver of light in the dark in Tenebrae Lux? sources.title: How To Solve All Main Puzzles In GTA 6′s Tenebrae Lux
sources.text: If you decide you’d rather sit at home all day and play a pretentious, cerebral puzzle game instead of go on heists, Tenebrae Lux is waiting for Jason and Lucia on their JoyStation in GTA VI . While on the surface it looks like just a funny gag poking at auteur culture (and one developer in particular), Tenebrae Lux is a surprisingly solid, short puzzle game that (if you’re not using this guide) may take you a few hours to get through. But I’m assuming you’re here because you either want to beat it quickly, or you’ve gotten so stuck (as I did) on a few of the puzzles that you’re desperate for help. I get you. Here’s as simple a walkthrough as I could manage for Tenebrae Lux : You’ll start out on the shoreline. You can’t do much: just walk around and examine objects. To start with, you’re going to want to head to the left side of the shore (assuming you’re facing the shore from the beach you start on) where there are multiple run-down shacks lit by big bright lights. Inside these shacks are three puzzles on gridded boards. On those grids, multiple pieces are placed with different 3D shapes atop: three-tiered tall ones, middling spiky ones, and flat ones with a tiny dot in the middle. The flat ones don’t move at all, the middle-sized spiky ones can slide across the board and clear the flat ones if they land next to them, and the three-tiered tall ones and middle-sized ones clear one another in the same fashion. Your goal is to clear all the pieces off the board. You can do these puzzles in any order. One of them is easy and straightforward, but the other two require a little bit more thinking. sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full". " Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it." Downing Street went on to address the issue of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters". The leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns . "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else." GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning" . We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it. This state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year ; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day . GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review .

sources.text: GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks like it's blocking them from progressing through the story while they wait for Sony and Rockstar to send out a fix. Although Rockstar Games spent a decade making its new Grand Theft Auto game, it's no surprise to see the new highest-rated game of all time launching with at least a few hiccups. Some have it worse than others, though, with more than a few reports of crashes affecting PS5 consoles popping up online in the days following GTA 6's launch. The most common cause seems to be tied to error code CE-108255-1, which, as defined by Sony , simply indicates that "an error occurred with the game/application." It seems that, although the majority of players aren't encountering the issue, those who have haven't been able to find a proper fix. Adding to the trouble is that those who have met these dreaded GTA 6 crashes are getting them pretty frequently, and what's triggering them isn't always clear. There are reports from players on both standard PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles running into these issues, with some even saying that crashes appear to be tied to the story, barring them from making any progress. "I've noticed that the issue manifests differently for different players," one Reddit user said . "In my case, the game crashes on Jason's loading screen: it freezes and then displays the CE-108255-1 error code, meaning I can't even get into the game. Others manage to play for a few minutes before experiencing a crash. I really hope Sony and Rockstar work together to investigate and resolve this issue as soon as possible." Game crashes are annoying for anyone, but when a massive game like GTA 6, which many feel has a less-than-generous autosave system , suddenly boots players back to the PS5 home screen without warning, it can be especially troublesome. Many who have reported the crashes to PlayStation Support say they've been directed to Rockstar, while those who report to Rockstar say they're being directed to PlayStation. One player said they feel like they're "stuck in an endless support loop, with a game I paid for and still can't play." Meanwhile, those who have managed to get help say most assistance hasn't been able to completely resolve their issues. However, some have said they've had luck with a few tried-and-true methods, such as uninstalling and reinstalling the game, making sure both the PS5 and game have their most recent updates, and restoring licenses. "I’ve done everything possible to solve this," another player said . "Deleted cache. Rebuilt database, deleted everything else from my console, took it apart, cleaned it, turned HDR off, switched to 1080p, went and updated game license, deleted and reinstalled and still crashing. Ugh. I’ve got a day 1 PS5 with a disc drive. Other friends of mine with the same console are playing with no issue." Again, it's unclear if the crashing issue is tied specifically to the PS5 or GTA 6 itself. Until either entity comes up with an update, though, all affected players are stuck on launch weekend. GTA 6 released for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19 and, in its first 24 hours, made Rockstar $3.79 billion. It's the most successful launch in the history of entertainment , and although its exact unit sales have yet to be disclosed, parent company Take-Two Interactive was at least willing to share that it sold 32.5 million copies in pre-orders alone. sources.text: Rockstar's hoping to innovate with Vice City's newest iteration Quote of the Day is a member-exclusive column here on GamesRadar+. Every day, we'll bring you a new talking point drawn from major industry interviews or our historic magazine archive. To get access to the entire collection, you can simply sign up to our free membership program below. If you're anything like me, you're planning on settling down to a long weekend of GTA 6 . But before you do, it might be worth hearing from Rockstar VP of design, Stephen Donkin, who says that Vice City represents a new kind of open world - one you shouldn't try and approach in the same way as a traditional game. "There is so much to do in Leonida," Donkin said in development notes supplied to press. "And so much to discover, that we hope players get to the point where they stop thinking in tasks, completion percentages, online guides, and rather let the game unfold in front of them." It's a bold ambition for players trained on at least a generation of games that do ask them to approach open worlds like a checklist, but Donkin has his reasons: "When you play the game and take your time with it, playing at the pace it asks you to, it can really unfold in front of you in a way that can feel almost infinite at a macro level, but each individual encounter still feels hand-crafted and with a human behind it," he says. "If players can let go and submit to becoming immersed in the world of Leonida, and just follow their nose as they play, they will feel the Leonida I have felt - and that's all we could ask for." This is actually one of the things that's making me most excited to experience GTA 6. The depth of some of its systems make it sound more like an RPG or even an immersive sim than the traditional action games that the previous games in the series have been, and getting a chance to invest in those slowly strikes me as the thing that's likely to set GTA 6 the furthest apart from similar titles. The type of game that doesn't direct you to its every corner in pursuit of some type of reward or checklist is few and far between, especially when you're talking about sprawling, open-world RPGs. The Witcher 3 and Breath of the Wild/Tears of the Kingdom come to mind, the latter in particular far more interested in getting you to play around with its tools than simply achieving set goals. But certainly there's been a trend of open world games that do the opposite - Assassin's Creed titles have long leaned towards completing tasks and collecting items. And in fact, Grand Theft Auto itself used to ask much more of the player in terms of collectibles and minigames if anyone wanted to attempt to 100% them. The likes of Vice City Stories and Liberty City Stories were much smaller games, but searching for red balloons and stray pigeons was something of a drag towards the end of the PS2 era. That GTA 6 is so deliberately shrugging that off is what could turn it into the next great open-world benchmark.
