sources.text: Tens of millions of people are playing Grand Theft Auto 6 right now . What’s the best way to experience Rockstar’s latest open-world epic? According to one of the developers themselves, you should play it with as little anxiety around checklists and online noise as possible. âThere is so much to do in Leonida, and so much to discover, that we hope players get to the point where they stop thinking in tasks, completion percentages, online guides and rather let the game unfold in front of them,” VP of design Stephen Donkin said in a packet of studio development notes shared with press. “When you play the game and take your time with it, playing at the pace it asks you to, it can really unfold in front of you in a way that can feel almost infinite at a macro level, but each individual encounter still feels hand-crafted and with a human behind it. Donkin’s first Rockstar credit was as a QA tester on GTA 5 , and his advice for GTA 6 players echoed the feelings of some of the studio’s other developers when it comes to taking in the immersive beauty and emergent nuance of the new entry’s complex world. âThere are clearly tons of high-stakes, high-energy, fast-paced moments and thrills and laughs along the way, but there are also quiet, meditative experiences and adventures to be had that offer a fully different feeling,” said senior design director Ghyan Koehne. “If I had to be held to a single feeling, Iâd say âwonder.â We want players to be constantly presented with a feeling of wonderâwe hope everyone feels a mixture of emotions.â It’s a stark contrast to how GTA lives in the popular imagination of most people, which is as a chaos sim full of drugs, sex, and violent crime. GTA 6 has those things, but they are far less domineering parts of the experience this time around. It’s also completely divorced from how some people often experience modern video games, which is heavily augmented by a second-screen experience full of achievement guides, TikTok memes, and social media rage-bait. People should play GTA 6 however they want, but I’d encourage them to take at least a few hours to experience the game in the dark with headphones on and as little knowledge as possible of what awaits them and how the whole thing works, their phones and laptops safely tucked away in a different room. Former Kotaku editor Kirk Hamilton was famous for telling people to turn off parts of the onscreen UI to make the experience more immersive and make it feel less like a chore list. Every big new open-world game that came out there would be a post about turning off the minimap . I’ve never been able to play games that way. I’m too fidgety and squirrely for that kind of thing. But I always try to spend at least a couple hours in that headspace, treating what’s in front of me more as something worth experiencing for its own sake than just as a maze to speedrun through as efficiently as possible in exchange for in-game rewards, entertaining setpieces, and satisfying emotional climaxes. That’s an increasingly alien way of approaching anything in our algorithmically optimized world, but GTA 6 offers as good a reason as any to try it. “If players can let go and submit to becoming immersed in the world of Leonida, and just follow their nose as they play, they will feel the Leonida I have felt,” Donkin said, “And thatâs all we could ask for.â Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. sources.text: Preorders of GTA 6 totalled approximately 32.5 million copies. Some very rough napkin math led to estimates that Take-Two Interactive expected to make as much as $3.5 billion during the Grand Theft Auto 6 launch period. It actually made more than that on the GTA 6 launch day: Rockstar says the game pulled in $3.79 billion in "day one retail sales," making it "the biggest entertainment launch in history." By way of comparison, Avengers: Endgame, ranked on Wikipedia as the highest grossing movie of all time, earned a little more than $2.9 billion over its entire theatrical run. GTA 6 crushed that by nearly $1 billion in a day . "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto 6," Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser said. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you." Strauss Zelnick, CEO of publisher Take-Two Interactive, had previously said that preorder levels of Grand Theft Auto 6 were "unprecedented" but declined to reveal specifics . It turns out he wasn't kidding: Take-Two Interactive also revealed today that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies in pre-release, which it said is "a new record across all platforms." Those numbers are absolutely staggering: There was never any question that GTA 6 was going to be huge, but those launch days sales—sales from one single day —surpass Take Two's net revenue guidance for the entire quarter by nearly $400 million at the high end. Given that there's still well over a month remaining in the holiday season, I'd expect that figure to rise significantly: I'm not an industry analyst but more than $4 billion before the year is over suddenly seems just about conservative. Beyond that, I won't even hazard a guess, but consider this: Grand Theft Auto 5 , which sold a little over 11 million copies on its launch day in 2013, has now surpassed 230 million copies sold in total. The sky, to paraphrase one of Tom Petty's other songs, really is the limit. sources.title: GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-sale copies and a bonkers $3.79 billion in its first day
sources.text: "We are incredibly humbled by the response." Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates. Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul. As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a new record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history." For context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles. "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," said Rockstar co-founder and company president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you." Previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water. Every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent company Take-Two previously said the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history . The only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't said anything concrete about that just yet. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review .

sources.text: Comcast has said GTA 6 's launch triggered the busiest traffic day the company has seen since it was founded in 1963. To put some of these numbers into perspective, the company shared a very relevant measurement. sources.name: IGN
sources.title: How a $6 Beer in GTA 6 Sent Me Into a Spiral of Crime and Anxiety
sources.text: I'm relationship-maxxing GTA 6. Forget the money, the cars, or building a criminal empire. My main aim is to make Jason and Lucia so disgustingly loved up that NPCs violently vomit as we walk past being all cute together. I want them to be the perfect couple. I want romance. I want devotion. I want the sort of relationship that makes everyone else in Vice City feel deeply inadequate. Unfortunately, the nuanced way GTA 6 tracks even the smallest actions has turned me into a paranoid lunatic, constantly worrying that one wrong move will destroy my carefully cultivated romance. Case in point: a $6 beer that sent me into a cascade of disasters, petty crime, and emotional turmoil, eventually ending with me restarting an entire mission because I was worried I'd blown it. Early on in the game, you're given the chance to prepare the house and complete some simple objectives ahead of picking Lucia up from prison. Naturally, I did them all. Fixed the steps, bought the necklace, got the flowers. I even made sure the car was dent-free, had a haircut and a shower, and dressed my Jason in his best jeans and shirt. My man was going to look presentable when he picked up the love of his life. I was on my best behavior. Nothing was going to stop me getting to my girl. In fact, I was so determined to be the perfect boyfriend that I even avoided committing any crimes on the way to the prison. In Grand Theft Auto. I obeyed traffic laws. I stopped at red lights. I avoided trouble wherever possible, to the point that when a random NPC tried to mug me, I just handed over my cash rather than risk getting into a fight. Remember that last part. It's important. After picking Lucia up from prison, you head straight to the Rusty Anchor for a few drinks. So far, so good. We've got the flowers, the necklace, the freshly showered boyfriend. This is going brilliantly. Then Lucia wanders off for a moment and asks Jason to get her a drink. Shit. I have no money. Suddenly, my decision to be a law-abiding citizen has come back to bite me in the arse. I gave all my money to a mugger because I was trying to be a good boyfriend, and now I can't afford to buy my girlfriend a beer. A beer that costs just $6. Surely this is a relationship test? If I follow Lucia without her drink, am I getting a little broken heart icon? Is this going into some invisible ledger of romantic failures? Have I already failed as a boyfriend, future husband, and potential co-parent because I can't produce one lousy alcoholic beverage? I start looking for solutions. I check every bottle in the bar, hoping I can just grab one and pretend I've paid for it. They're all empty. I search the entire building for something I could quickly pawn, like a trading card, or even just some random cash someone has carelessly left lying around. Nothing. The panic is setting in. I head outside and start searching the nearby streets. I don't want a wanted rating, because surely being arrested while Lucia waits patiently for a drink isn't going to do wonders for our relationship either. So I look for cars with trunks I can break into easily. I find a selection of sunglasses and hats, which is lovely, but unless Lucia has suddenly developed a taste for drinking accessories, they're not going to help me. I'm now seriously considering mugging someone. I only need $6. Six. Dollars. That's barely a crime, right? In the grand scheme of GTA, that's practically community service. I pull out my gun and start advancing on a random NPC walking down the sidewalk. I'm about to threaten an innocent stranger with a deadly weapon so I can buy my girlfriend a beer. This is what love looks like, apparently. And then it happens. The game suddenly switches to a cutscene of Lucia saying, "You forgot about me?" NO. NO! The opposite! I was thinking about you the entire time! I needed $6 for a beer, light of my life! I was prepared to commit armed robbery for you! Does that mean nothing? But the damage is done. Or at least, I think the damage is done, which is somehow worse. Has the game registered that I wandered off and abandoned Lucia? Does she think Jason is an inconsiderate arsehole? Have I just knocked several invisible points off my perfect relationship score? Is this going to come back to haunt me 30 hours from now when she remembers that time I left her alone in a bar? I can't take the risk. I restart the checkpoint. Unfortunately, this creates another problem. The checkpoint puts me right outside the prison, which means I still have no money. I've travelled back in time, but I haven't solved the fundamental issue of being a broke boyfriend. Luckily, there's a parking lot nearby. This time, I abandon my commitment to good behaviour. I go rogue, breaking open trunks left and right, ignoring alarms and grabbing whatever I can get my hands on. The same man who was carefully obeying traffic laws 20 minutes ago is now systematically robbing parked cars in broad daylight. Eventually, I walk away with $30. A fortune. Five beers' worth of romantic security. I get Lucia her drink. Crisis averted. Relationship saved. Probably. And that's the thing about GTA 6 that's completely got its hooks into me. I've become so thoroughly relationship-pilled that I'm making decisions I would never normally consider in a Grand Theft Auto game. I'm not thinking about how much money I can make, how many cars I can steal, or how much chaos I can cause. I'm thinking about whether Jason is being a good boyfriend. I'm worrying about whether Lucia feels appreciated. I'm committing crimes not for personal gain, but in the service of being a thoughtful romantic partner. It's ridiculous, but it's also fascinating. Rockstar has somehow made me care about the smallest interactions between these two characters to the point where I'm second-guessing everything I do. The possibility that an apparently insignificant action might have consequences for their relationship is enough to make even buying a beer feel like a high-stakes

sources.title: Learn how to get a mask in GTA 6 to stay anonymous when committing a crime
sources.text: Learning how to buy, manage, and equip a mask in GTA 6 is vital for losing some of your Appearance Heat If you want to be a better criminal in Leonida, you're going to need to learn how to get a mask in GTA 6. Despite Rockstar making appearance a key factor in the new Wanted system, the game isn't super clear on the steps you can take to hide your identity – particularly as you're progressing through Chapter 1 of the GTA 6 missions list . Thankfully, I'm here to help you understand how to get neckwear in GTA 6 , how to equip masks, and how to change them for new ones. You can buy a mask in GTA 6 from any of the gun stores. Chuck's Tackle & Shot in Key Lento sells them (look at the central stand with the alligator head atop of it) from the beginning of the game, but you can head to any Ammu-Nation retailer to find more. Open up the GTA 6 Index , head into the weapons tab, and you'll be able to find all the relevant shops on your map. When you begin exploring Vice City and Vice Beach, you'll also find thrift stores that sell novelty masks, and high-end retailers which sell very fancy (and expensive) coverings that can be worn as well. To wear a mask in GTA 6, you need to make sure that it's with you. You can add neckwear items to your loadout by visiting the wardrobe in your residences. Scroll to the accessories tab and that's where you'll find the Masks option, which separates them by brand. If you want options while you're on the road, you can also store some in the trunk of your personal vehicle in GTA 6 by highlighting it and pressing Square/X. With a mask in your loadout, wearing it is as simple as holding L1/LB to open your loadout. Press R1/RB to scroll to the items menu, and then select Mask from the neckwear slot located at twelve-o'clock in the wheel. Press A to put it on, press A to remove it. Easy enough, and vital if you want to lose some of your Appearance Heat after robbing a store with CCTV equipment. While hovering over the neckwear slot of your loadout, you can also press up and down to change the wear style of your mask in GTA 6. The first will see the mask conceal your face, which will draw panicked reactions from shop clerks, while the second will let you fashion the mask more appropriately. sources.title: How to turn off GTA 6 auto uploads on Xbox
sources.text: You could risk a ban by auto-uploading GTA 6 clips to the Xbox Network If you're playing GTA 6 on Xbox, you should turn off your console's automatic upload feature or you could risk having your Xbox account suspended. An Xbox user on Reddit reported receiving a two-day, unrepealable ban for automatically uploading a 28-second clip of GTA 6 characters at the beach. According to the Reddit user, sangobar, the clip was almost immediately flagged by the Xbox Network for either violating the Xbox Community Standards or Microsoft Services Agreement terms (the email they received from Xbox doesn't specify which). However, the user claims the clip only showed characters in beachwear and the clip was therefore incorrectly flagged. So, to avoid the risk of an Xbox ban it is better to be safe than sorry, to disable your Xbox automatic upload feature, and to understand what Xbox's guidelines are around the content you can upload to the Xbox Network. Automatic uploads to the Xbox Network are enabled as standard on Xbox, meaning the GTA 6 clips you capture on your console are automatically uploaded to the Xbox Network. To turn off your Xbox Series X's automatic uploads feature, follow these steps: One Drive is more lenient in what you can upload, but if you'd rather not automatically upload any of your GTA 6 capture, it's best to set both it and Xbox Network to 'Don't Upload'. GTA 6 clips could potentially violate the 'Keep your content clean' term of the Xbox Community Standards , specifically the 'Make stuff that's suitable for all audiences rule', which states: "The Xbox community must be friendly and accessible to everyone, this isn't the appropriate place for sexual content. Keep your public posts and messages suitable for all ages and audiences." According to Xbox, some examples of content that could violate this term include sharing or distributing non-consensual intimate imagery, links or imagery that displays pornography, screenshots or game clips that include mature sexual content, custom gamerpics that contains nudity, lewd messages to other players, and distasteful or inappropriate pictures. In other words, be careful before sharing images or clips of GTA 6's more mature content, like GTA 6 strip clubs . © GamesRadar+. Not to be reproduced without permission. sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 's auto drive feature is perfect if you just want to see the sights of Leonida or avoid navigating through traffic. Not that GTA 6 goes out of its way to tell you there even is an auto drive feature. It's tucked away in a menu you have little cause to use early in the game, and you also need to make sure a specific setting is toggled on for it to work in some circumstances. It's best to still learn how to drive decently yourself, though, as auto drive isn't the best choice in hectic situations. Below, we explain how to auto drive in GTA 6 and when you'd want to take the wheel yourself. Autodrive is enabled automatically from the start, but only for safe scenarios. If you want to use it whenever, here's what to do. The next time you're in a vehicle, do this to use auto drive: To turn auto drive off, you just need to hold down on the D-pad again. Auto drive does what you'd expect. It handles the driving — or flying or sailing — for you, and it avoids accidents, road rage, manslaughter, crashed planes, and all the other problems you might get yourself into if you were driving manually. You don't have to set a destination for it to work, though if you do set one, it'll take you there. The game enters cinematic mode and takes camera control from you, though you can still enter photo mode from the pause menu if you want to rotate the camera for a shot. You also still have control over the radio. Just make sure you familiarize yourself with GTA 6 's driving in between the bouts of cinematic vibes tourism. In unrestricted mode, you can use auto drive in "unsafe" scenarios like chase or escape missions, of which there are quite a few. You kind of don't want to, though. Knowledge of side streets, learning how to handle a sharp turn at speed, and a deft hand at avoiding collisions (or causing strategic ones) can make a big difference in these sequences. Aut odrive also won't save you from damage or other issues you started before enabling it. It'll get you out of tight situations, like bad parking, but it might cause some damage to the surrounding area and your car in the process. sources.title: Arknights: Endfield version update ‘Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms’ launches November 25
sources.text: Publisher GRYPHLINE and developer Mountain Contour will release the version update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms” for free-to-play 3D RPG Arknights: Endfield on November 25, the companies announced. The game’s latest live stream also introduced the upcoming version 2.0 update, which takes players to Gypsosia and aboard the Rhodes Island landship, and teased 10 characters who will join the journey across upcoming content updates. “With Wuling’s story wrapping up, and the main story taking us through all the heavy moments, we want to give you a change of pace with a lighthearted, upbeat update,” said Arknights: Endfield producer Light Zhong in a press release. Here is an overview of the update, via GRYPHLINE: Version Update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms” Strange mushrooms have overrun an abandoned dam outside Wuling, where Landbreakers worship a giant mushroom and visitors keep slipping into hallucinations. There, the Endministrator meets Kay, a Rhodes Island Operator who has been adventuring alone across Talos-II in search of them. Kay happily shares everything she treasures, including a towering stack of honey waffles. But which would she choose: a mountain of waffles or a dear friend? A Nature Vanguard with a carefree fighting style, Kay throws weapons that scatter across the battlefield, then gathers them up for a heavy hammer slam. Along the way, she drops Picnic Snacks that heal her teammates. The Old Dam, the update’s new area, has grown into a fairytale-like mushroom kingdom. Players fire Kay’s honey waffles at mushrooms to open doors and spin fungal bridges, and must avoid Loquacious Shrooms that scramble their sense of direction. Mushroom foes like the Bolete Prince guard the dam, and a mushroom as tall as a mountain waits at its heart. The update’s music leans into its whimsical tone, with Ori composer Gareth Coker and ambient producer Owsey returning to score Kay’s honey waffle adventure. It caps a first year in which the soundtrack has followed the story, from the sweeping sci-fi orchestral sound of Valley IV to the choir-driven battle against Alleikhreos, Typhoeus’s JRPG-inspired winter journey and the modern electronic take on Eastern music in Si’s painted world. Later in the update, every player who logs in during the Workers’ Guards: Roll Call event will receive the Operator Mimino and her signature weapon, Star of Tomorrow, for free, with event missions offering extra copies to reach full Potential. Operators Gilberta and Rossi also return in successive reruns. For factory builders, Exclusion Zone Rebuilding is a new permanent mode in which players supply materials across four phases to restore the North Wuling Exclusion Zone, using the new Forge of Luminance to transform products on their conveyor belts. For a lighter break, Lucky Carrot’s Games of Wonder adds two multiplayer card games, Witch’s Darkjack and Band Uprising, that players can enjoy with friends or through matchmaking. A First Look at Version 2.0 and Rhodes Island The livestream also previewed the next chapter of Arknights: Endfield , arriving in the new year. Exiles have launched attacks across the Civilization Band, and their real target is Rhodes Island. The Endministrator sets out with Perlica into Gypsosia, the Cretaceous Frontiers, where players will be able to board and explore Rhodes Island itself, a massive landship. A 10-character teaser offered a glimpse of companions for the journey, including Warfarin, appearing as the leader of Rhodes Island, and M3, who returns looking completely different. The chapter’s first update will add four new maps at once, including Rhodes Island. Main Mission Early Unlock: Gypsosia will let players who have completed the main mission Remediation Progress skip ahead to the new story while still earning all beginner-event rewards. New modes are also in development for future updates, including a management sim with the Golden Branch Tribe and the Shattered Protocol combat mode. Arknights: Endfield is now Steam Deck Verified, with default controller support and every feature available on Valve’s handheld. The update also brings Despot Weaponized, a new high-difficulty challenge series in Umbral Monument; the return of RISE! MEGA ARENA!, a two-Operator arena event; and new seasons of the Echoes of War combat mode. Arknights: Endfield is available now for PlayStation 5 , PC via the official launcher, Steam , and Epic Games Store , iOS via App Store , and Android via Google Play .
